S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of difficulties with sustaining attention, organization, and follow-through that cause impairment across settings, without prominent hyperactive or impulsive behaviors. Symptoms typically begin in childhood, though functional impact may become more evident later when environmental demands increase, such as in higher-level schooling or complex work roles. The course is usually chronic, with some individuals developing compensatory strategies that can partially mask deficits until life stressors or cognitive load exceed their coping capacity. It is distinguished from anxiety, mood, and cognitive disorders by its early onset, trait-like inattention across contexts, and lack of primary memory loss or fluctuating consciousness.

patient.personality: Christopher is a socially outgoing, competitively driven young man who enjoys challenges and improvising solutions but tends to be casual about planning and structure.
patient.stressor: About a year and a month ago, Christopher was moved from a more routine filing role into a position that required frequent data entry, cross-checking documents, and managing several small projects at once for multiple supervisors. He initially welcomed the challenge and relied on his energy and competitiveness to stay ahead of deadlines, but the increased volume of fine-grained paperwork, shifting priorities, and ad hoc requests made it harder for him to rely on memory and informal systems. As he tried to balance longer workdays with late-night gaming, social activities, and weekend volunteer events, the accumulation of small administrative tasks began to outstrip his loosely structured approach to planning. After being called out for repeated minor errors in spreadsheets and forms that affected coworkers’ work, and noticing similar lapses in everyday tasks like managing bills and errands, he decided to see a psychiatrist to figure out why he kept making simple mistakes despite feeling motivated and capable.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep making simple mistakes on forms and spreadsheets at work, even when I think I’ve double-checked them.”

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: At work I’ll swear I’ve gone through a spreadsheet carefully, but then my supervisor points out I typed a number in the wrong column or skipped a whole line, just dumb little things that I somehow don’t notice even on a ‘double-check.’

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: People will be talking to me at my desk, giving me instructions, and halfway through I realize my brain has drifted off to thinking about a game or my weekend plans, and I have to ask them to repeat what they just said because it didn’t really register.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: Since I started this new role, when I look at my to‑do list with tasks from three different bosses, I just kind of freeze and bounce between them randomly, so I end up rushing at the end of the day because I didn’t plan out what to tackle first.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly patting my pockets or digging through my backpack at work because I’ve set down my access card, a USB drive, or a specific folder somewhere and can’t remember where I put it five minutes ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: I’ll be entering data and then a Slack notification pops up or I hear a conversation down the hall, and next thing I know I’ve clicked over to a browser tab or I’m just staring into space thinking about something else instead of finishing the form.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: When I’m stuck in long meetings or sitting at my computer for hours, I feel this restless energy in my legs and keep shifting in my chair or drumming my fingers because it’s really hard to just sit still and focus the whole time.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even when I try to relax, like reading or watching a quiet show, I get bored and fidgety after a few minutes and end up grabbing my phone, turning on loud music, or switching to a fast‑paced game because just doing one calm thing feels uncomfortable.
